newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: China's Zhu sees 8.0 pct growth into next century.
newsitem.headline: China's Zhu sees 8.0 pct growth into next century.

text.p: Chinese vice premier and economic tsar Zhu Rongji on Saturday painted a robust picture of the Chinese economy, forecasting eight percent or higher growth and inflation under five percent "well into the next century".

Speaking at a dinner in Perth to Australian business and political leaders, Zhu said China's adoption of open market reforms in the past decade had secured an average annual growth rate of nine percent since 1979.
"In the past several years the figure stands at around nearly 10 percent," Zhu said through an interpreter.
"After overcoming the overheated economy before 1993, we have successfully brought inflation rates down to 6.1 percent last year and 2.2 percent from January to April this year," he said.

"We have every reason to believe that China's economy will be able to maintain a growth rate of eight percent and even higher, and will be able to control the inflation rate below five percent, and that this trend of development will last well into the next century."
Zhu, credited with China's rapid economic growth and a key force in the restructuring of state businesses, also forecast another "bumper" agricultual harvest this year.
"In the past two years China has had a very bumper agricultural harvest and we expect to have another good harvest this year," Zhu said.
Zhu said China would achieve self-sufficiency in food supplies, but did not give a timeframe and added that it would continue to buy wheat from Australia.
China is Australia's fifth largest trading partner, with two-way trade worth A$8.0 ($6.12) billion in calendar 1996.
Trade is growing about 20 percent a year and China is projected to move to Australia's number two trading partner, behind Japan, by 2005.
Zhu arrived in Australia on Friday for a week-long, landmark visit to cement improved ties and reward Canberra for an easing of its stand on human rights in China.

Australia-China relations chilled last year with a series of diplomatic and security spats and Australian officials said Zhu's week-long visit would not only focus on trade and investment, but repairing bilateral relations.
Zhu will meet Australian Prime Minister John Howard next week in Canberra. ($ = 1.305 Australian Dollars)
